definition_zh: 测量；量出；尺寸；措施；分寸；程度；节拍；格律
definition_en: to find the size or amount of something; a step taken to deal with a problem; a standard or a degree of something
core_image: 一把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出的数字被写进料单，旁边压着一张应对步骤的便签
scene: 木工把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出长度，再把数字写在料单上。Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：测定某物的尺寸或数量；句意为木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、桌沿、料单、铅笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 测量；量出；估量
尺寸；量度；措施；分寸；（音乐的）小节；格律

senses.title: To find a size or amount
senses.definition: to find the size, length, weight or amount of something by using a tool or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 用工具或标准求出某物的尺寸、长度、重量或数量
senses.example: Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
senses.exampleCN: 木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to measure, and the physical act of comparing against a standard is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本意就是测量，拿某物与标准相比较的实体动作是最古老的一层。

senses.title: The number obtained
senses.definition: the size or amount that a measurement produces, often written as a figure with a unit
senses.definitionCN: 测量得出的尺寸或数量，常写成带单位的数字
senses.example: The measure came out at two metres, not one.
senses.exampleCN: 量出来的结果是一点九米，不是一米。
senses.why: A measurement is both the act and its outcome, so the noun carries the number as well as the procedure.
senses.whyCN: 测量既是动作也是结果，因此这个名词既携带数字，也携带过程。

senses.title: A step taken to fix something
senses.titleCN: 为解决问题所采取的步骤
senses.definition: an action or policy adopted to deal with a problem or to reach an aim
senses.definitionCN: 为处理问题或达到目的而采取的行动或政策
senses.example: The city took measures to cut traffic at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 市里采取措施减少校门口的交通。
senses.why: A step is a measured amount of action: enough to change the situation, not more, and the metaphor runs from dose to policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个步骤就是定量的行动：足以改变局面，又不过量，这个比喻从剂量一直走到政策。

senses.title: A proposed law
senses.definition: in a legislature, a proposed law put forward for debate and vote
senses.definitionCN: 在立法机构中提交辩论与表决的法律草案
senses.example: The measure passed by three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票之差通过。
senses.why: A bill is a measured response written into legal form, and American usage kept the word for the draft itself.
senses.whyCN: 法案是把有分寸的应对写成法律形式，美式用法保留了这个词来指草案本身。

senses.title: A standard for comparison
senses.definition: a standard, unit or benchmark by which other things are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断其他事物的标准、单位或基准
senses.example: Test scores are a crude measure of a school.
senses.exampleCN: 考试分数是对学校的一种粗略衡量。
senses.why: To measure anything one needs a fixed unit, and the noun then names any yardstick, including an abstract one.
senses.whyCN: 要测量任何东西都需要固定单位，名词随后指任何标尺，包括抽象的标尺。

senses.title: A degree or extent
senses.definition: the extent to which something is true or present, as in in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 某事物为真或存在的程度，如「在很大程度上」
senses.example: The success was in large measure due to the technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 这次成功在很大程度上要归功于技术人员。
senses.why: An amount can be spoken of without a ruler, so the word extends from physical quantity to degree of influence.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以不用尺子来说，于是这个词从物理量扩展到影响的程度。

senses.title: A limit or moderation
senses.definition: a proper limit in behaviour or feeling, or the absence of one in beyond measure
senses.definitionCN: 行为或情感上应有的限度，或在「无法估量」中表示没有限度
senses.example: His anger went beyond measure.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒到了无法估量的地步。
senses.why: The idea of a fixed amount turns moral: to keep measure is to keep within bounds, and to exceed it is to lose proportion.
senses.whyCN: 固定数量的观念转向道德：守分寸就是守在界限内，越过就是失去比例。

senses.title: A bar in music
senses.definition: a group of beats between two bar lines, the unit of musical time
senses.definitionCN: 两条小节线之间的一组拍子，是音乐时间的基本单位
senses.example: The phrase fits one measure of four beats.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐句正好占一小节四拍。
senses.why: Music divides time into equal measured spans, so the word for measuring became the name of the span.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把时间分成等长的段，于是表示测量的词成了那一段的名字。

senses.title: The metre of a line
senses.definition: the patterned rhythm of a line of verse, counted in feet
senses.definitionCN: 诗句中有规律的节奏，以音步计数
senses.example: The poem keeps a steady measure through twelve lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗十二行都保持稳定的格律。
senses.why: Verse counts syllables the way a ruler counts inches, and the noun for the count became the name of the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 诗句像尺子量英寸那样数音节，表示计数的名词就成了这种模式的名字。

intro.en: Measure comes from Old French mesure, from Latin mensura 'a measuring', built on metiri 'to measure'. The root is generally connected with a very old word for measure that also gave Greek metron and English metre.
intro.cn: measure 来自古法语 mesure，源头是拉丁语 mensura「测量」，由 metiri「测量」构成。这个词根一般认为与一个极古老的「度量」词相关，希腊语 metron 与英语 metre 也出自它。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure or apportion, and it is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: metiri 意为测量、按量分配，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Mensura named the act and the result of measuring, and it passed through French as the English noun.
items.cn: mensura 指测量的动作与结果，经法语成为英语名词。

items.en: The old root is generally reconstructed as a word for measure, the same one behind metre and metric; the reconstruction is accepted but the exact shape is source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个古老词根一般被重构为表示「度量」的词，metre 与 metric 也出自它；这一重构被接受，但确切形态来源不确定。

items.en: Old French mesure carried both the physical and the moral senses, and English took the pair together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mesure 同时带有物理与道德两层意思，英语在十三世纪把两者一起接收。

items.en: American usage of the eighteenth century applied measure to a proposed law, a use that British English largely dropped.
items.cn: 十八世纪的美式用法把这个词用到法律草案上，英式英语后来大体放弃了这一用法。

items.en: Latin mensura had already named the counted span in rhythm, and English kept measure for a bar and for metrical pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mensura 早已用来指节奏中被数出的段落，英语保留 measure 指小节与格律。

note.en: The first group shares the measuring root; the second group names related actions or quantities.
note.cn: 第一组共享「测量」词根；第二组是相关动作或数量。

entries.definition: The act or the figure produced by measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 测量的动作，或测量得出的数字。

entries.definition: Large or stable enough to be measured.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或稳定到可以被测量的。

entries.definition: Deliberate and restrained, as if each step were weighed.
entries.definitionCN: 审慎而有节制的，仿佛每一步都称过。

entries.definition: The process, or a compound for a tool such as a measuring tape.
entries.definitionCN: 测量过程，或构成卷尺一类工具名。

entries.definition: The mathematics of lengths, areas and volumes; a learned doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的数学；学术性的同源词。

entries.definition: To estimate or measure, often with an instrument; also the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 估计或测量，常借助仪器；也指该仪器。

entries.definition: To express something as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物表示为数字。

entries.definition: To judge the value or level of something, with less emphasis on units.
entries.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或水平，对单位的强调较少。

entries.definition: An action taken toward a goal, the everyday word behind the policy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目标而采取的行动，是政策义背后的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin measuring verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of policy and tools.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语测量动词、真实同族词，以及政策与工具里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin metiri meant to measure, and mensura gave English the noun through French.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，mensura 经法语给了英语这个名词。

normal.en: The family runs measure, measurement, measurable, measured and measuring.
normal.cn: 同族词有 measure、measurement、measurable、measured 与 measuring。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: take measures, safety measures, in large measure, beyond measure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：采取措施、安全措施、在很大程度上、无法估量地。

normal.en: A tape measure is the tool, and a measure of success is the standard: one word, two kinds of ruler.
normal.cn: 卷尺是工具，衡量成功的标准是标尺：同一个词，两种尺。

normal.en: Music counts beats into a measure, and verse counts feet into a measure.
normal.cn: 音乐把拍子数成小节，诗句把音步数成格律。

abstract.en: To keep measure is to know how much is enough, which is a moral skill before it is a mathematical one.
abstract.cn: 守分寸就是知道多少算够，这先是道德的技能，然后才是数学的。

abstract.en: What can be measured is not always what matters, and what matters is not always measurable.
abstract.cn: 可测量的不总是重要的，重要的也不总是可测量的。

abstract.en: A measure is a decision about what counts, made before any number appears.
abstract.cn: 尺度是在数字出现之前，关于「什么算数」的决定。

examples.en: The nurse measured the wound and wrote the figure in the chart.
examples.cn: 护士量了伤口的大小，把数字写进病历。

examples.en: The council adopted three measures to reduce waste.
examples.cn: 议会通过三项措施减少浪费。

examples.en: Her patience was tested beyond measure that afternoon.
examples.cn: 那天下午，她的耐心受到了无法估量的考验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「米热」——用尺子一点点比过去，看看到底有多长：测量

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「测量、量度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure。词根一般认为与古希腊语 metron 同源，确切形态属重构，来源不确定；法案、小节与格律义均为后起扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one ruler: the act of measuring, the number it gives, a policy step, a bill, a standard, a degree of influence, a moral limit, a musical bar and a line's metre.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一把尺：测量的动作、量出的数字、政策步骤、法案、比较标准、影响程度、道德限度、音乐小节与诗句格律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape is laid along the desk, and the number goes straight onto the cutting list.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺贴住桌沿，数字直接写进下料单。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE FIGURE: laying a tape down, and the number that comes back.
branches.cn: 动作与数字：把尺子贴上去，以及报回来的那个数。

branches.en: THE POLICY DOSE: a step sized to the problem, and the same step written as a bill.
branches.cn: 政策剂量：按问题大小配出的步骤，以及写成法案的同一步骤。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: test scores used as a crude ruler for a school.
branches.cn: 标尺：把考试分数当作衡量学校的粗尺。

branches.en: THE DEGREE AND THE LIMIT: influence measured in large part, anger that passes all bounds.
branches.cn: 程度与限度：占很大部分的影响，与越过一切界限的愤怒。

branches.en: THE COUNTED SPAN: four beats between two bar lines, feet counted through a line of verse.
branches.cn: 被数出的段落：两条小节线之间的四拍，与一行诗里数出的音步。

intro.en: Measure is a Latin noun and verb of measuring, and the family keeps both the physical tool and the abstract standard.
intro.cn: measure 是拉丁语中表示测量的名词与动词，其词族同时保留实体工具与抽象标准两面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is metiri, mensura and the adjective mensurabilis, with French mesure as the carrier into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 metiri、mensura 与形容词 mensurabilis，古法语 mesure 则是进入英语的载体。

items.example: The noun carries both the act and the standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时携带动作与标准。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: It named both the act and its result.
It builds nouns of outcome, as in mensura.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结果的词，如 mensura。

items.example: French added the moral sense of keeping within bounds.
items.exampleCN: 法语加上了守界限的道德含义。

items.meaning: the act or result of measuring
items.example: The English suffix names the process.
The suffix marks possibility.
The participle turned the noun into a manner.
items.exampleCN: 分词把名词变成了举止。

items.example: The negative suffix marks what cannot be counted.
items.exampleCN: 否定词尾标出无法计数之物。

items.example: The learned doublet stays close to Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个学术同源词紧贴拉丁语。

latinEntries.structure: Latin deponent verb metiri (met-, mensus; to measure)
latinEntries.example: Latin metiri means to measure or allot.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量、分配。

latinEntries.example: Latin mensura means a measuring, and gives English measure.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 mensura 意为测量，并给出英语 measure。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun suffix -ura (result of an action)

latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -ura 构成 cultura（耕作）这类名词。
拉丁语 mensurabilis 意为可测量的。

definition_zh: 测量；测量结果；尺寸；度量单位体系；测定方法；评估；身体尺寸；测量误差；测量数据
definition_en: the act or process of measuring something, the figure or size obtained, or a system of units used for measuring
core_image: 木匠把卷尺拉过木板，把读数写进小本子
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉过木板，把量得的数字写进本子。The carpenter pulls the tape across the board and writes the number in his notebook: that number is one measurement.
sceneCN: 这里 measurement 是「测得的尺寸」（第 2 个义项：测量结果）；句意：木匠把卷尺拉过木板，把那个数字写进本子，这个数字就是一次测量结果。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、木板、笔记本、铅笔、刻度数字；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 测量；测量结果；尺寸；度量体系；测定方法

forms.label: 单数（一次测量或测量这件事）
复数（多处尺寸或多组数据）

senses.title: The act of measuring: taking a reading
senses.definition: the act or process of finding the size, amount or extent of something with an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器求出某物大小、数量或延展的过程
senses.example: Careful measurement of the sample took an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细测量这个样本花了一小时。
senses.why: The suffix -ment, from Latin -mentum, names the act or its product. This first sense keeps the act: the tape is stretched and a value is sought.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 出自拉丁语 -mentum，表示动作或其产物。第一个义项保留动作义：卷尺被拉开，人们要找一个数值。

senses.title: The result: a figure or size obtained
senses.titleCN: 测量结果：得到的数字或尺寸
senses.definition: the figure, size or amount obtained by measuring
senses.definitionCN: 测量得到的数字、尺寸或数量
senses.example: The measurements show a room of about thirty square metres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量结果显示这个房间约三十平方米。
senses.why: The same suffix also names what the act leaves behind. Once the tape is folded away, the number remains, and that number is also called a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也指动作留下的东西。卷尺收起来之后，数字仍然在，这个数字同样叫 measurement。

senses.title: A system of units used for measuring
senses.titleCN: 度量体系：用于测量的单位系统
senses.definition: a system of units and standards by which quantities are expressed, such as the metric system
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示数量的单位与标准体系，如公制
senses.example: The laboratory converted all readings to the metric system of measurement.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把所有读数都换算成公制计量体系。
senses.why: A number means nothing without a unit. The word therefore also names the shared scale itself, the system that makes readings comparable between labs and countries.
senses.whyCN: 没有单位，数字毫无意义。因此这个词也指共享的尺度本身，即让不同实验室、不同国家的读数可以互比的那套体系。

senses.title: The method or instrument used to measure
senses.titleCN: 测定方法：用何种手段量
senses.definition: the technique or instrument by which a quantity is determined, as in a measurement technique
senses.definitionCN: 确定某一数量的技术或仪器，如某种测量技术
senses.example: They changed the measurement method to reduce noise in the data.
senses.exampleCN: 他们改换了测量方法以减少数据中的噪声。
senses.why: The word moves from the act to the means of the act. Asking about 'the measurement used' is asking which procedure produced the number.
senses.whyCN: 词从动作转到动作的手段。问「用的是什么测量」，问的就是哪个流程产出了这个数字。

senses.title: Assessment: measuring performance or quality
senses.titleCN: 评估：把表现或质量当成量来测
senses.definition: the assessment of performance, quality or progress as if it were a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 把表现、质量或进展当作数量来评估
senses.example: Measurement of teacher performance is itself controversial.
senses.exampleCN: 对教师表现的评估本身就很有争议。
senses.why: What cannot be held with a tape can still be treated as a quantity. The word extends from physical size to judgement, and keeps the authority of the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 卷尺量不了的东西仍可被当作数量来处理。这个词从物理尺寸延伸到判断，同时保留了仪器的权威感。

senses.title: Body measurements: sizes taken for clothing
senses.titleCN: 身体尺寸：做衣服时量的三围
senses.definition: the set of body sizes taken with a tape, used for making or buying clothes
senses.definitionCN: 用软尺量出的一组身体尺寸，用于做衣或买衣
senses.example: The tailor took my measurements before cutting the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝在裁布之前先量了我的尺寸。
senses.why: Here measurements is plural because a body yields several figures. The word keeps its plain physical sense but names a set rather than a single value.
senses.whyCN: 这里用复数，因为一具身体会得到好几个数字。词仍保留朴素的物理义，只是指一组值而非单个值。

senses.title: Precision measurement: readings and their error
senses.titleCN: 精密计量：读数与它的误差
senses.definition: the technical process of obtaining precise values, considered together with instrument error and uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 获得精确数值的技术过程，并连同仪器误差与不确定度一起考虑
senses.example: Every measurement carries an uncertainty that must be reported.
senses.exampleCN: 每次测量都带有一个必须报告的不确定度。
senses.why: In metrology the word names a physical process with limits. Since no instrument is perfect, a measurement is always a value plus an admitted range of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 在计量学中，这个词指一个有极限的物理过程。仪器都不完美，所以测量永远是数值加上一个被承认的误差范围。

senses.title: Recorded readings: the data set
senses.titleCN: 测量数据：记录下来的一整套读数
senses.definition: the recorded set of readings taken during an experiment or survey
senses.definitionCN: 在一次实验或调查中记录下来的一整套读数
senses.example: The raw measurements were stored before any analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 原始测量数据在任何分析之前先被存了下来。
senses.why: Once readings are written down they become data. The plural then names a collection, and the word sits between the act of measuring and the analysis that follows.
senses.whyCN: 读数一旦写下就成了数据。复数于是指一个集合，而这个词正处在测量动作与随后分析之间的位置上。

intro.en: Measurement is the English noun measure plus -ment, from Latin -mentum, which names an act or its result. Measure came into English in the 14th century through Old French mesure from Latin mensura, the noun of metiri 'to measure'. The compound measurement is recorded in the 18th century, when scientific instruments made repeated readings a routine matter. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: measurement 是英语名词 measure 加 -ment，后者出自拉丁语 -mentum，表示动作或其结果。measure 在 14 世纪经古法语 mesure 进入英语，源自拉丁语 mensura，即 metiri「测量」的名词。measurement 这一复合形式在 18 世纪见于记载，当时科学仪器使反复读数成为常规。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Metric conventions and national standards bureaus make measurement a public, regulated activity rather than a craftsman's habit.
items.cn: 公制惯例与各国标准局的建立，使测量从工匠的习惯变成公共的、受规范的活动。

items.en: English measurement is recorded, formed from measure plus -ment as instruments and experiments spread.
items.cn: 英语 measurement 见于记载，随仪器与实验的普及由 measure 加 -ment 构成。

items.en: measure is borrowed through Old French mesure and covers a unit, a limit and the act of measuring.
items.cn: measure 经古法语 mesure 借入，兼指单位、限度与测量行为。

items.en: mensura is the noun of metiri; the same verb gives dimension, commensurate and immense.
items.cn: mensura 是 metiri 的名词形式；同一个动词还给出 dimension、commensurate、immense。

items.en: metiri rests on the reconstructed root *med- 'to measure, take the right size', which also gives modus and hence mode and moderate.
items.cn: metiri 建立在重构词根 *med-「测量、取恰当尺寸」上，该词根也给出 modus，进而有 mode 与 moderate。

note.en: The first group separates true relatives from a word that merely looks technical; the second compares words used in neighbouring parts of the same task.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与只是看起来专业的词分开；第二组比较同一件事相邻环节上的词。

entries.definition: the verb 'to find the size of' and the noun for a unit, limit or legislative step. Measurement is only the act or result, while measure also names the standard and the policy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「测量」，名词指单位、限度或立法措施。measurement 只指动作或结果，而 measure 还指标准与政策措施。

entries.definition: the branch of geometry dealing with lengths, areas and volumes, or the act of measuring in a formal sense. It is the learned Latin-style counterpart, confined to technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的几何分支，或正式意义上的测量行为。它是学术性的拉丁式对应词，只用于技术写作。

entries.definition: a measurable extent such as length, width or height. It comes from dis- plus metiri, so it shares the measuring verb but names an extent rather than the act of measuring it.
entries.definitionCN: 可测量的延展，如长、宽、高。它由 dis- 加 metiri 构成，共享「测量」这个动词，但指延展本身，而不是测量的动作。

entries.definition: the act of judging the value or quality of something. It overlaps the figurative sense of measurement but does not require numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物价值或质量的判断。它与 measurement 的引申义重叠，但不要求有数字。

entries.definition: the figure shown by an instrument at a moment. It is one measurement in the narrowest sense, taken off a dial or a display.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器在某一刻显示的数字。它是最狭义的一次测量，取自表盘或显示屏。

entries.definition: a defined indicator used to judge performance. It is a measurement chosen for a purpose, where measurement is the general obtaining of values.
entries.definitionCN: 用于评判表现的确定指标。它是为某个目的选定的测量，而 measurement 是一般的取值过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ment gives both faces of the word: the act of measuring and the figure that the act leaves behind.
normal.cn: -ment 给出这个词的两面：测量的动作，以及动作留下的数字。

normal.en: measure is the verb and the general noun; measurement is specifically the act or the result, never the policy.
normal.cn: measure 是动词兼一般名词；measurement 专指动作或结果，从不指政策措施。

normal.en: A measurement without a unit is just a number, which is why the word also names the system of units.
normal.cn: 没有单位的测量只是一个数字，所以这个词也指单位体系。

normal.en: The plural measurements usually means a set: body sizes, or a table of readings from an experiment.
normal.cn: 复数 measurements 通常指一个集合：身体尺寸，或实验读出的一整表数值。

normal.en: Measurement error is not a mistake but the admitted uncertainty that comes with every instrument.
normal.cn: measurement error（测量误差）不是错误，而是每件仪器都带来的、被承认的不确定度。

abstract.en: See a tape stretched, a number written, and a unit agreed: the three parts of every measurement.
abstract.cn: 想象卷尺拉开、数字写下、单位约定：这就是每次测量的三个部分。

abstract.en: The word travels from hand to page to report, and loses nothing but gains a claim to objectivity.
abstract.cn: 这个词从手上走到纸面再走到报告，什么也没丢，却获得了一种客观性的主张。

abstract.en: Whenever someone says 'by measurement', ask which instrument and which unit did the speaking.
abstract.cn: 每当有人说「按测量」，就该问：是哪件仪器、哪个单位在说话。

examples.en: Repeated measurement reduced the effect of random error.
examples.cn: 反复测量减小了随机误差的影响。

examples.en: The engineer sent the measurements to the factory.
examples.cn: 工程师把尺寸数据发给了工厂。

examples.en: Their claim rests on a single measurement taken at noon.
examples.cn: 他们的结论建立在正午所做的一次测量上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没辙门特」——没辙时也得把门特（门）量一遍 → measurement 测量、尺寸

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「尺度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure；加 -ment（拉丁 -mentum，表示动作或结果）→ measurement。核心是「量这一动作，以及量出来的那个数」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a tape pulled across something. What changes is which part of the event is named — the pulling, the number, the agreed unit, the method, the judgement, the body being fitted, the error, or the whole table of readings.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一条卷尺拉过某物。变化的只是命名了这件事的哪一段——拉尺的动作、数字、约定的单位、方法、判断、被量身的身体、误差，还是整张读数表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter's tape stretched across a board, the figure written down.
core.cn: 核心意象：木匠的卷尺拉过木板，数字被写下来。

branches.en: THE ACT: the tape is stretched and a value is sought, which is measuring as an activity.
branches.cn: 动作：卷尺拉开去找一个值，这就是作为活动的测量。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: one figure, or the whole recorded table of figures left after the act.
branches.cn: 产物：单个数字，或动作结束后留下的整张记录表。

branches.en: THE SHARED SCALE: units and standards make one lab's number comparable with another's.
branches.cn: 共享尺度：单位与标准让一个实验室的数字可与另一个实验室的比较。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT AND ITS LIMIT: the method produces the value, and every method brings its own uncertainty.
branches.cn: 仪器及其极限：方法产出数值，而每种方法都带来自己的不确定度。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE JUDGEMENT: sizes taken for a suit, and performance treated as if it could be measured.
branches.cn: 身体与判断：为做衣量出的尺寸，以及被当作可测量的表现。

intro.en: Measurement is measure plus -ment, from Latin -mentum. That suffix names an act (as in movement) or its result (as in document), and measurement uses both faces.
intro.cn: measurement 是 measure 加 -ment，出自拉丁语 -mentum。这个后缀表示动作（如 movement「移动」）或其结果（如 document「文件」），measurement 两面都用上了。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is metiri 'to measure' with its noun mensura. The suffix -mentum also appears in document, monument and argument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 metiri「测量」及其名词 mensura。后缀 -mentum 也见于 document「文件」、monument「纪念碑」、argument「论点」。

items.meaning: the act of measuring, or the figure obtained
items.example: The measurement was repeated three times.

items.meaning: to find the size of, or a unit, limit or step
items.meaningCN: 测量；亦指单位、限度或措施
items.example: They measured the depth of the well.
The gain was measurable within a month.
items.exampleCN: 一个月内就有了可测的增益。

items.example: The room grew measurably quieter.
The measurability of pain is limited.
items.exampleCN: 疼痛的可测性是有限的。

items.meaning: having no limits that can be measured
items.meaningCN: 无边无际的；无法计量的
items.example: They crossed a measureless plain.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片无边无际的平原。

items.structure: the same noun used for the technical process
items.meaning: the regulated process of obtaining values with instruments
items.meaningCN: 用仪器取得数值的规范过程
items.example: Measurement standards protect trade.

items.meaning: the formal or geometric measuring of lengths, areas and volumes
items.meaningCN: 测量术；几何中的长度面积体积计算
items.example: Mensuration is taught with areas and volumes.
items.exampleCN: 测量术是随面积与体积一起教的。

items.meaning: a measured extent such as length
items.example: Length is one dimension of the box.
items.exampleCN: 长度是这个箱子的一个维度。

items.meaning: measured by the same standard, and so proportionate
items.example: The fine was commensurate with the damage.

latinEntries.meaning: forms nouns of action or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词

definition_zh: 肉；食用肉；（果实或坚果的）可食部分；实质；要旨
definition_en: the flesh of animals eaten as food, the soft edible part inside fruit or nuts, or the central substance of something
core_image: 一块放在砧板上的肉，旁边是敲开的坚果，露出里面饱满的果仁
scene: 冬天的炖锅在灶上咕嘟作响，屋里飘着香料味。She added a little salt to the meat and left it to simmer.
sceneCN: 这里是「供食用的肉」（第 1 个义项：动物肉作为食物）；句意为她往肉里加了一点盐，让它慢慢炖。

pos.zh: 肉；食用肉；实质

derivatives.zh: 由 meat 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「多肉的；内容丰富的」
由 meat 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无肉的」
由 meat 与 ball 复合而成，义为「肉丸」

senses.title: Animal flesh used as food
senses.definition: the flesh of animals, especially cattle, pigs and sheep, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 尤指牛、猪、羊等动物供人食用的肉
senses.example: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
senses.exampleCN: 屠夫把肉切成薄片。
senses.why: Old English mete meant food of any kind; as other foods took their own names, the general word narrowed onto the flesh sold at a butcher's stall.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mete 泛指任何食物；随着其他食物各自有了名字，这个宽泛的词就收窄到肉铺案板上出售的肉。

senses.title: The edible soft part of fruit or nuts
senses.definition: the soft or fleshy part inside a fruit, nut or shell that can be eaten
senses.definitionCN: 水果、坚果或壳内可供食用的柔软部分
senses.example: Crack the shell and scoop out the meat of the walnut.
senses.exampleCN: 敲开壳，把核桃仁挖出来。
senses.why: The idea of the edible inside of a thing was already present in food, so the word was extended to the part of a nut or fruit worth eating.
senses.whyCN: 「某物内部可食的部分」这一想法本就包含在「食物」里，于是词义被扩展到坚果或水果里值得吃的那一部分。

senses.title: The central substance of an idea or text
senses.definition: the most important part or central content of an argument, book or plan
senses.definitionCN: 论点、书或计划中最重要的部分、核心内容
senses.example: The meat of the report is in its final three pages.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的要旨就在最后三页。
senses.why: If flesh is what fills a body, then the substantial part of a text can be called its meat, with the rest treated as bone or wrapping.
senses.whyCN: 如果肉是填满身体的东西，那么一篇文章的实质部分也可以叫它的 meat，其余部分则被看成骨头或包装。

senses.title: Food of any kind, in older usage
senses.definition: solid food in general, the older sense still visible in a few fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 泛指固体食物，这一较古的词义仍残留在少数固定短语中
senses.example: In older English, meat could mean any food a household stored.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的英语里，meat 可以指一户人家储存的任何食物。
senses.why: This is the original sense; it survives mainly in old texts and in the fixed phrase meat and drink, while everyday usage keeps only the flesh sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的词义；它主要残存在旧文本与固定短语 meat and drink 里，日常用法只保留了「肉」这一义项。

intro.en: Meat began as a general word for food and narrowed to animal flesh, a shift whose exact cause is not settled.
intro.cn: meat 起初是泛指食物的词，后来收窄为动物肉，这一变化的确切原因尚无定论。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *matiz meant food, and its earlier origin is uncertain; no reliable Latin cognate is recorded.
items.cn: 重构名词 *matiz 意为食物，其更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.en: Old English mete meant food or nourishment of any kind, not flesh in particular.
items.cn: 古英语 mete 泛指食物或营养，并不专指肉。

items.en: Middle English kept the broad sense, and meat could still name bread, fruit or drink in the same sentence.
items.cn: 中古英语保留宽泛的词义，meat 仍可与面包、水果或饮料并列。

items.en: Usage narrowed towards animal flesh, though scholars do not agree on a single cause for the change.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄到动物肉，不过学者对变化的确切原因并无一致结论。

items.en: The flesh sense dominates, while the older idea survives in compounds and in the figurative sense of substance.
items.cn: 「肉」的义项占主导，较古的词义则保存在复合词与「实质」的比喻义里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the flesh family and one word that merely sounds the same; the near-meaning group collects names for flesh and for kinds of meat.
note.cn: 形近组收「肉」这一族词，外加一个只是读音相同的词；近义组收表示肉与各种肉类的词。

entries.definition: Full of meat, or rich and substantial in content.
entries.definitionCN: 多肉的；内容丰富的。

entries.definition: A ball of minced meat cooked in sauce or soup.
entries.definitionCN: 用肉末做成、在酱汁或汤里煮的丸子。

entries.definition: Made or eaten without meat.
entries.definitionCN: 不含肉或以无肉方式食用的。

entries.definition: To come together with someone; only the sound and spelling are close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人会面；只是读音和拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The soft body tissue of a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物身上的软组织。

entries.definition: Meat from cattle, a specific kind of red meat.
entries.definitionCN: 牛肉，一种具体的红肉。

entries.definition: Meat from pigs.
entries.definitionCN: 猪肉。

entries.definition: Wild animals hunted for food, or their meat.
entries.definitionCN: 供食用的野味或其肉。

normalIntro.en: The word started wide and ended narrow, and the old width still shows in a few compounds and in the sense of substance.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从宽泛起步、以狭窄收场，旧日的宽泛仍体现在少数复合词与「实质」义里。

normal.en: Old English mete was a general word for food, so the ancestor of meat had nothing to do with animals.
normal.cn: 古英语 mete 是泛指食物的词，所以 meat 的祖先与动物无关。

normal.en: The narrowing to flesh happened gradually, and nobody can point to one single cause.
normal.cn: 收窄为「肉」是逐渐发生的，没有人能指出唯一的原因。

normal.en: The adjective meaty adds -y, and meatless adds -less, two small endings that show the flesh sense clearly.
normal.cn: 形容词 meaty 加 -y，meatless 加 -less，两个小后缀清楚显示了「肉」的义项。

normal.en: Meatball is a plain compound: meat plus ball, the shape named directly.
normal.cn: meatball 是直白的复合词：meat 加 ball，直接以形状命名。

normal.en: The meat of a walnut or the meat of an argument keeps the old idea of the edible or substantial inside.
normal.cn: 核桃的 meat 或论点的 meat，都保留了「内部可食或实质部分」的旧想法。

abstract.en: Picture a butcher's block: the word food shrank until it fit exactly on that block.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肉铺的砧板：food 这个词不断缩小，直到正好落在砧板上。

abstract.en: Every language has words that start wide and end narrow, and meat is one of the clearest examples.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都有由宽变窄的词，meat 就是最清楚的例子之一。

abstract.en: Cut a nut open and the same word appears again, this time for the good part inside.
abstract.cn: 把坚果切开，同一个词又出现了，这次指里面最好的那部分。

examples.en: She added a little salt to the meat and left it to simmer.
examples.cn: 她往肉里加了一点盐，让它慢慢炖。

examples.en: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
examples.cn: 屠夫把肉切成薄片。

examples.en: The meat of the report is in its final three pages.
examples.cn: 报告的要旨就在最后三页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蜜特」——烤肉抹上蜜特别香；记住 meat 是肉，也可指实质。

root: 古英语 mete（泛指食物），出自原始日耳曼语 *matiz（食物），更早来源不确定，未见可靠的拉丁同族词；词义后来收窄为「动物肉」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the edible part of a body; the senses move from animal flesh to the inside of a nut and finally to the substance of an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是身体上可食的部分；义项从动物肉移到坚果内部，最后移到论点的实质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut of meat on a block beside a cracked nut showing its kernel.
core.cn: 核心意象：砧板上的一块肉，旁边是敲开的坚果，露出果仁。

branches.en: a butcher slicing a joint on a block
branches.cn: 屠夫在砧板上切一大块肉

branches.en: a cracked walnut with its kernel exposed
branches.cn: 敲开的核桃露出果仁

branches.en: a reader underlining the last pages
branches.cn: 读者在最后几页画线

branches.en: an old kitchen storing bread and drink
branches.cn: 老厨房里存着面包和饮料

branches.en: the same word for a steak and for an argument
branches.cn: 同一个词既指牛排也指论点

intro.en: The entry is supported by an Old English food noun, its Germanic source, two productive suffixes and two everyday compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词条由古英语的食物名词、它的日耳曼语来源、两个能产后缀和两个日常复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for meat; Latin carō, the word for flesh, is a synonym rather than a relative.
latinIntro.cn: meat 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 carō 表示「肉」，只是近义词而非同源词。

definition_zh: 机械装置；机械结构；机制；机理；途径
definition_en: a set of connected moving parts, or an abstract arrangement of parts and processes that produces a particular result
core_image: 一排咬合的齿轮：每一枚只做一件事，连起来却推动整台机器
scene: 钟表匠掀开旧钟的后板，让里面的构件露出来。The clockmaker lifted the back plate to show the mechanism of the old tower clock.
sceneCN: 这里 mechanism 是「机械结构、传动装置」（第 2 个义项：机器内部一起工作的部件与结构）；句意：钟表匠揭开后板，展示这座老塔钟的机械结构。场景要点：塔钟的黄铜后板、层层咬合的齿轮、钟表匠手里的放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 机械装置；机械结构；传动部件
机制；机理；途径；方法

derivatives.zh: 机械的；机械式的；呆板的
机械论的；用机械式因果解释的

senses.title: A set of moving parts
senses.definition: the parts of a device that move together to perform a particular action
senses.definitionCN: 装置中一起运动、完成特定动作的那些部件
senses.example: The locking mechanism jammed after years of use.
senses.exampleCN: 使用多年之后，锁具装置卡住了。
senses.why: Greek mēkhanē named a device, and the first English sense was the structure of a machine. The physical set of parts is the core image in its most concrete form.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mēkhanē 指装置，英语最早的义项就是机器的结构。这一套实体部件，就是核心意象最具体的形态。

senses.title: The working structure inside a machine
senses.definition: the arrangement and interaction of a machine's parts, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 机器各部件作为整体时的排列与相互作用
senses.example: He explained the mechanism of the clock, gear by gear.
senses.exampleCN: 他一个齿轮一个齿轮地讲解这座钟的机械结构。
senses.why: Once the parts are seen together, attention shifts from the pieces to how they transmit motion. The word now names the logic inside the device.
senses.whyCN: 当部件被放在一起看，注意力就从零件本身转到它们如何传递运动。这个词于是命名装置内部的那套逻辑。

senses.title: An institutional mechanism
senses.definition: an established arrangement of rules, offices, and procedures that produces a result or handles a problem
senses.definitionCN: 由规则、机构和程序构成的既定安排，用来产生某种结果或处理某个问题
senses.example: The treaty set up a mechanism for settling border disputes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约建立了一套解决边界争端的机制。
senses.why: Institutions can be read as parts of a machine: each office turns one wheel, and the arrangement yields a decision. The physical picture is applied to procedure.
senses.whyCN: 制度可以被读成机器的零件：每个机构带动一只轮子，整套安排产出一个决定。物理画面被套用到了程序上。

senses.title: A biological mechanism
senses.definition: a set of bodily or cellular processes that produces a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 身体或细胞层面的一组过程，产生特定效果
senses.example: The immune mechanism recognises the virus within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 免疫机制在数小时内就识别出这种病毒。
senses.why: A living body also has interlocking parts, though they are cells and signals rather than gears. The image survives because the result still depends on the parts acting in order.
senses.whyCN: 活的躯体也有相互咬合的部件，只不过它们是细胞与信号，而不是齿轮。意象仍然成立，因为结果依旧依赖各部件按次序行动。

senses.title: A psychological mechanism
senses.definition: a repeated mental process by which a person copes with feelings or situations
senses.definitionCN: 一个人用来应对情绪或处境的、反复出现的心理过程
senses.example: Mocking others can work as a defence mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 嘲笑别人可以起到防御机制的作用。
senses.why: The mind is treated as an apparatus with parts: a feeling enters, a routine process turns it, and a behaviour comes out. The word lends machinery to psychology.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作一台有部件的装置：一种情绪进入，一套惯常过程把它转动，一种行为出来。这个词把机械感借给了心理学。

senses.title: A reaction mechanism in chemistry
senses.definition: the step-by-step sequence by which reactants become products, including intermediate states
senses.definitionCN: 反应物变成产物的逐步序列，包括中间状态
senses.example: The reaction mechanism involves two short-lived intermediates.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应机理涉及两种寿命很短的中间体。
senses.why: A reaction is a process with stages, and each stage hands the matter on to the next like one gear driving another. The word names the hidden chain.
senses.whyCN: 反应是一个分阶段的过程，每一阶段把物质交给下一阶段，就像一只齿轮带动另一只。这个词命名的正是那条看不见的链条。

senses.title: The philosophical doctrine of mechanism
senses.definition: the view that natural events can be explained entirely by the motion of matter, without purpose or vital force
senses.definitionCN: 认为自然事件完全可以由物质运动来解释、无需目的或生命力 的观点
senses.example: Mechanism holds that life can be explained by matter and motion alone.
senses.exampleCN: 机械论认为生命仅凭物质与运动就能得到解释。
senses.why: Here the metaphor is taken all the way: the whole of nature is declared to be one machine. The word stops naming a device and starts naming a world view.
senses.whyCN: 这里把比喻推到了底：整个自然被宣告为一台机器。这个词不再命名某个装置，而开始命名一种世界观。

senses.title: A means or channel for doing something
senses.definition: a method, channel, or route through which something can be done
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事所经由的方法、渠道或途径
senses.example: The committee has no mechanism for enforcing its decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会没有执行其决定的机制。
senses.why: If a result is produced by parts working in order, then any such arrangement is a way to get the result. The concrete device thins into 'means'.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果由部件按次序工作产生，那么任何这样的安排都是取得结果的一条路。具体装置于是淡化成“手段”。

intro.en: Mechanism came into English in the 1660s from Modern Latin mechanismus, built on Greek mēkhanē 'machine, device'. The Greek-to-Latin route is clear; the deeper Indo-European link is disputed.
intro.cn: mechanism 于 17 世纪 60 年代由现代拉丁语 mechanismus 进入英语，后者建立在希腊语 mēkhanē“机械、装置”之上。希腊语到拉丁语的路径清楚；更深的印欧语关联存在争议。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'the structure of a machine, engine, or other contrivance for controlling or utilizing natural forces'. The source is Modern Latin mechanismus.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 60 年代，意为“机器、引擎或其他用来控制或利用自然力的装置的结构”。来源是现代拉丁语 mechanismus。

items.en: The broader sense 'a mechanical contrivance or agency of any kind' is recorded. From here the word begins to detach from literal hardware and to name any working arrangement.
items.cn: 较宽的义项“任何种类的机械装置或作用机构”有记录。自此这个词开始脱离字面上的硬件，用来命名任何一套运作安排。

items.en: Mechanismus was formed from Greek mēkhanē plus the Latin noun suffix -ismus. It is a scholarly coinage, not an inherited Latin word.
items.cn: mechanismus 由希腊语 mēkhanē 加拉丁名词后缀 -ismus 构成。它是学术性的新造词，不是继承下来的拉丁词。

items.en: Greek mēkhanē, with the Doric variant makhana, meant 'device, tool, machine', and also 'contrivance, cunning'. It is the source of machine and mechanic as well as mechanism.
items.cn: 希腊语 mēkhanē（多里斯方言作 makhana）意为“装置、工具、机械”，也有“计谋、机巧”的意思。它既是 machine、mechanic 的来源，也是 mechanism 的来源。

items.en: Watkins derived mēkhanē from PIE *magh- 'to be able, have power', the root behind may, might and magic. Beekes rejects this on formal grounds and treats the Greek word as Pre-Greek, so the deepest root is disputed and best marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 沃特金斯把 mēkhanē 追溯到原始印欧语 *magh-“能够、有力量”，该词根也是 may、might、magic 的来源。比克斯从形式证据上反对这一联系，认为这个希腊词属于前希腊语底层，因此最深词源有争议，宜标为来源不确定。

items.en: Mechanic, mechanical, mechanics, mechanize and mechanistic all belong to the same family. Mechanism keeps two lives: a concrete device, and an abstract system of parts and processes.
items.cn: mechanic、mechanical、mechanics、mechanize、mechanistic 都属于同一词族。mechanism 保有两条命：一个是具体装置，一个是由部件与过程构成的抽象系统。

note.en: The first group separates the whole machine, the mass noun, the person and the adjective. The second group compares mechanism with apparatus, device, process and system.
note.cn: 第一组区分整台机器、集合名词、人和形容词；第二组把 mechanism 与 apparatus、device、process、system 作比较。

entries.definition: a complete device with moving parts that does a job. Mechanism is the arrangement inside such a device, or the abstract version of that arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 一台有活动部件、能完成某项工作的完整装置。mechanism 是这种装置内部的排列，或这种排列的抽象版本。

entries.definition: machines as a group, or the moving parts of a machine taken as a mass. It is uncountable, while a mechanism is one countable arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 机器的总称，或作为整体看的一台机器的活动部件。它不可数，而 mechanism 是一套可数的排列。

entries.definition: a person who repairs or operates machines. It names a worker, not the working arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 修理或操作机器的人。它命名的是工人，而不是运作的结构。

entries.definition: explaining things as if they were produced by machinery. It describes a view or style, not a device.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物当作由机械产生来解释的。它描述一种观点或风格，而不是一件装置。

entries.definition: a set of equipment assembled for a particular purpose, often scientific. It names the whole set-up, while mechanism stresses how the parts work together.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的组装的一套设备，常用于科学场景。它命名整套装备，而 mechanism 强调部件如何一起运作。

entries.definition: an object invented to do a particular job. A device is what it is; a mechanism is how it works.
entries.definitionCN: 为完成特定工作而发明的物件。device 说的是“它是什么”，mechanism 说的是“它怎样运作”。

entries.definition: a series of actions that leads to a result. It gives the order of stages; mechanism adds the interlocking parts that carry the stages out.
entries.definitionCN: 导向结果的一系列行动。它给出阶段的顺序；mechanism 则补上执行这些阶段的咬合部件。

entries.definition: an organized set of parts or rules. It is broader than mechanism: a system may be social or biological, and it need not have a visible causal chain.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的部件或规则集合。它比 mechanism 更宽：系统可以是社会的或生物的，也不必有可见的因果链。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek mēkhanē 'device', machine and mechanic, and the modern family mechanical / mechanics / mechanize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 mēkhanē“装置”，machine 与 mechanic，以及现代词族 mechanical／mechanics／mechanize。

normal.en: Greek mēkhanē meant 'device, tool, machine'. Mechanism is the Latin-built noun for the way such a device is put together.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mēkhanē 意为“装置、工具、机械”。mechanism 是拉丁语构造的名词，指这种装置被组装起来的方式。

normal.en: Machine, mechanic and mechanism share one Greek source. The machine is the whole object, the mechanic is the person, and the mechanism is the working arrangement.
normal.cn: machine、mechanic、mechanism 共享同一个希腊来源。机器是整体物件，技师是人，机制则是运作的排列。

normal.en: Mechanical is the adjective, mechanics is the science of forces and motion, and mechanize is to replace hands with machinery.
normal.cn: mechanical 是形容词，mechanics 是研究力与运动的科学，mechanize 则是用机械取代人手。

normal.en: A defence mechanism, a reaction mechanism and a market mechanism all keep the same picture: parts in contact, each turning the next.
normal.cn: 防御机制、反应机理与市场机制都保留同一幅画面：部件相互接触，每一枚带动下一枚。

normal.en: Mechanistic is the adjective for a view that treats everything as machinery; it is a judgement about an explanation, not a description of a device.
normal.cn: mechanistic 是形容词，指把一切当作机械的看法；它是对某种解释的评判，而不是对装置的描述。

abstract.en: Picture a row of gears. No single gear can do the job alone; the result appears only when each one passes motion to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一排齿轮。没有任何一只齿轮能独自完成工作；只有当每一只把运动传给下一只，结果才出现。

abstract.en: A mechanism is a way of hiding the work: you see a handle turn, but the useful result happens inside the box.
abstract.cn: 机制是一种把劳动藏起来的方式：你看见手柄在转，真正有用的结果却发生在盒子内部。

abstract.en: The same word serves a lock, an immune system and a treaty because all three produce a result through parts that depend on one another.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能用于一把锁、一套免疫系统和一项条约，因为这三者都通过彼此依赖的部件产出一个结果。

examples.en: The engineer traced the fault to a worn cam in the valve mechanism.
examples.cn: 工程师把故障追查到阀门装置里一只磨损的凸轮。

examples.en: Scientists still argue about the exact mechanism by which the drug works.
examples.cn: 科学家仍在争论这种药起效的确切机理。

examples.en: The two countries agreed on a mechanism for sharing river water.
examples.cn: 两国就共享河水的一套机制达成了一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦克你怎”——麦克，你怎把这一排齿轮装进盒子？→ mechanism 机械装置、机制

root: 源自希腊语 mēkhanē“机械、装置”，经现代拉丁语 mechanismus 进入英语，核心是“一组咬合部件按次序把运动传下去”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of mechanism, all from one picture: interlocking parts, each doing one small job, together producing a result — whether the parts are gears, cells, institutions, or steps in a reaction.
sensesIntro.cn: mechanism 的八个义项都来自同一幅画面：相互咬合的部件，每个只做一件小事，合起来产出一个结果——无论这些部件是齿轮、细胞、机构，还是反应中的步骤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of interlocking gears, each passing motion to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排咬合的齿轮，每一只把运动传给下一只。

branches.en: HARDWARE: a lock or a clock is a set of parts, and the mechanism is both the parts and the way they move together.
branches.cn: 硬件：一把锁或一座钟是一套部件，mechanism 既是这些部件，也是它们一起运动的方式。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENTS AND MEANS: institutions and procedures can be arranged like parts, and any such arrangement is a way to get a result.
branches.cn: 安排与手段：机构与程序可以像部件一样被安排，而任何这样的安排都是取得结果的一条路。

branches.en: LIFE AND MIND: immune responses and defence routines are hidden processes whose parts still depend on one another.
branches.cn: 生命与心灵：免疫反应与防御套路都是隐藏的过程，其部件同样彼此依赖。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: a reaction mechanism is the step-by-step chain that turns reactants into products.
branches.cn: 化学：反应机理是把反应物变成产物的逐步链条。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: mechanism turns the metaphor into a world view, declaring all of nature to be one machine.
branches.cn: 哲学：机械论把比喻提升为世界观，宣告整个自然就是一台机器。

intro.en: Mechanism is Greek mēkhanē fitted with a Latin noun suffix. English then adds -ical, -ics, -ize and -ation, and the same Greek root also gives machine and machinery.
intro.cn: mechanism 是希腊语 mēkhanē 装上拉丁名词后缀构成的。英语随后加上 -ical、-ics、-ize、-ation，同一个希腊词根还给出 machine 与 machinery。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin mechanismus is a scholarly compound of Greek mēkhanē and Latin -ismus. Latin also borrowed the Greek noun as machina, which is the direct source of English machine and machinery.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁语 mechanismus 是希腊语 mēkhanē 与拉丁后缀 -ismus 的学术复合词。拉丁语还把希腊名词借作 machina，这正是英语 machine 与 machinery 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a working arrangement of parts; a system that produces a result
items.meaningCN: 部件的运作排列；产生结果的机制（mēkhanē 装置 + -ismus 名词后缀）
items.example: The clock's mechanism needs cleaning every year.
items.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械结构每年都要清洗。

items.example: The body uses several mechanisms to control heat.
items.exampleCN: 身体用好几套机制来控制体温。

items.meaning: explaining things as if by machinery
items.meaningCN: 机械论的；机械式解释的（-istic 构成形容词）
items.example: A mechanistic view leaves no room for purpose.
items.exampleCN: 机械论的观点不给目的留下空间。

items.meaning: to replace manual work with machinery
items.meaningCN: 使机械化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The farm mechanized harvesting in the 1950s.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场在 20 世纪 50 年代实现了收割机械化。

items.meaningCN: 机械化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Mechanization cut the need for seasonal labour.
items.exampleCN: 机械化减少了对季节性劳动力的需求。

items.meaning: working by machinery; done without thought
items.meaningCN: 机械的；机械式的；呆板的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The lift stopped because of a mechanical fault.
items.exampleCN: 电梯因机械故障停了下来。

items.meaning: by means of machinery; without thought
items.meaningCN: 机械地；用机械方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She answered mechanically, without listening.
items.exampleCN: 她机械地回答，根本没在听。

items.meaning: the science of forces and motion; the way something works
items.meaningCN: 力学；机械学；运作方式（-ics 表示学科）
items.example: The mechanics of the trade are taught in the first term.
items.exampleCN: 这门行业的具体运作方式在第一学期教授。

items.meaningCN: 机械师；修理工（拉丁语 mechanicus，源自希腊语）
items.example: The mechanic replaced the worn bearing.
items.exampleCN: 修理工更换了磨损的轴承。

items.meaning: a device with moving parts that does work
items.meaningCN: 机器（拉丁语 machina，源自希腊语 mēkhanē）
items.example: The machine prints two thousand labels an hour.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器每小时印两千张标签。

items.meaning: machines as a group; the working parts of a machine
items.meaningCN: 机器总称；机器的运转部件（-ery 构成集合名词）
items.example: The factory replaced its old machinery.

items.meaning: a prefix meaning mechanical or machine-related
items.meaningCN: 表示“机械的、与机械有关的”构词成分
items.example: A mechanoreceptor responds to touch or pressure.
items.exampleCN: 机械感受器对触碰或压力作出反应。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 机器的结构（现代拉丁语新造词）

latinEntries.meaning: mechanical; a person skilled in machines

definition_zh: 医疗的；医学的；内科的；身体状况的；（名词）体检
definition_en: relating to the practice, profession or study of medicine, to treatment that is not surgical, or to a person's health and health records
core_image: 白大褂口袋里露出一截听诊器，背后夹着一叠病历
scene: 她车里放着急救箱，包里带着医院的病历。She kept a medical kit in the car and a copy of her hospital records in her bag.
sceneCN: 这里 medical 是「医疗的、医学的」（第 1 个义项：属于医疗职业与医学学科）；句意：她在车里放着医药箱，包里带着一份病历复印件。场景要点：一只白色药箱、一叠写满记录的纸、袋口露出的听诊器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 医疗的；医学的；内科的；与健康状况有关的
体检（英式口语，medical examination 的缩略）

forms.label: 名词复数（“体检”义；形容词无屈折）

derivatives.zh: 医生；医学生；战地卫生员

senses.title: Of the profession
senses.titleCN: 医疗职业与学科：属于医生这一行
senses.definition: relating to the profession, practice or study of medicine
senses.definitionCN: 与医学职业、医疗实践或医学学科有关的
senses.example: She applied to three medical schools and was accepted by two.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了三所医学院，被其中两所录取。
senses.why: Medical entered English in the 1640s from Late Latin medicalis, 'of a physician', from medicus 'physician'. The adjective first names whatever belongs to doctors.
senses.whyCN: medical 于 17 世纪 40 年代从晚期拉丁语 medicalis 进入英语，意为“医生的”，源自 medicus“医生”。这个形容词最初用来命名一切属于医生的东西。

senses.title: Medical versus surgical
senses.titleCN: 内科的：与外科相对的那一半
senses.definition: relating to treatment by drugs and other non-surgical means, as opposed to surgery
senses.definitionCN: 指以药物及其他非手术手段进行的治疗，与外科相对
senses.example: He was moved from the surgical ward to the medical ward for observation.
senses.exampleCN: 他从外科病房转到内科病房接受观察。
senses.why: Inside one profession, medical marks the branch that treats with medicine rather than the knife. The word draws a line within the hospital, not outside it.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个行业内部，medical 标记的是用药物而不是用刀的那一支。这个词画的是医院内部的界线，而不是对外的界线。

senses.title: The patient's condition
senses.titleCN: 身体状况与病史：属于这个人的健康
senses.definition: relating to a person's health, illnesses and physical condition
senses.definitionCN: 与某人的健康、疾病和身体状况有关的
senses.example: The form asks for your medical history and any allergies.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表格要求填写你的病史和过敏情况。
senses.why: The adjective shifts from the profession to the patient: what belongs to the physician's domain becomes the record of a body's past.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从职业转到病人身上：原本属于医生领域的东西，变成了一个身体过往的记录。

senses.title: A medical: the check-up
senses.titleCN: 体检：形容词被剪成一个名词
senses.definition: a medical examination
senses.definitionCN: 体检；医学检查
senses.example: He passed his medical and joined the crew in March.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过了体检，三月加入了船员队伍。
senses.why: Recorded from 1917 as a shortening of medical examination. English often clips a familiar adjective-plus-noun phrase into the adjective alone.
senses.whyCN: 1917 年起有记录，是 medical examination 的缩略。英语常把熟悉的“形容词加名词”词组剪成只剩形容词。

senses.title: A medical: the doctor
senses.titleCN: 医学生、医生：旧时的口语名词
senses.definition: in older colloquial use, a medical student or a doctor
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中指医科学生或医生
senses.example: The old novels speak of a medical coming to the house at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 旧小说里常写一位医生半夜上门。
senses.why: The noun use is recorded from 1823. A person is named by what he or she studies or practises, so the adjective stands alone as a human subject.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法自 1823 年有记录。人被以他所学或所做的事来称呼，于是这个形容词单独站出来指人。

senses.title: Medical evidence
senses.titleCN: 法律与保险中的医学鉴定
senses.definition: used of reports, evidence and certificates that come from doctors and carry legal or official weight
senses.definitionCN: 指来自医生、具有法律或官方效力的报告、证据与证明
senses.example: The court ordered a medical report before deciding on the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在裁定索赔之前下令出具一份医学报告。
senses.why: Once medicine enters law, its documents become evidence. Medical marks the source of authority behind the paper.
senses.whyCN: 一旦医学进入法律，它的文书就成了证据。medical 标记的是这张纸背后的权威来源。

senses.title: Medical equipment
senses.titleCN: 器械与技术：复合词里的限定语
senses.definition: used in compounds for equipment, imaging and technology employed in health care
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，指医疗照护中使用的设备、影像与技术
senses.example: The charity shipped medical supplies and two portable ultrasound machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构运去了医疗物资和两台便携超声仪。
senses.why: As a classifying adjective it can attach to any object used in care, from a glove to a scanner, without changing its own meaning.
senses.whyCN: 作为分类形容词，它可以附着在任何用于照护的物件上，从手套到扫描仪，而自身含义不变。

senses.title: Medical leave
senses.titleCN: 病假与证明：制度里的一个类别
senses.definition: used in employment contexts for leave or certificates that excuse absence because of illness
senses.definitionCN: 用于雇佣语境，指因病请假或证明缺勤正当的证明文件
senses.example: She took five days of medical leave after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后她请了五天病假。
senses.why: Institutions need a word for absence backed by a doctor. Medical turns an illness into a recognised administrative category.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个词来指“有医生作保的缺勤”。medical 把一场病变成一个被承认的行政类别。

senses.title: Medical, not medicinal
senses.titleCN: 与 medicinal 的分界：说用途，不说药效
senses.definition: describing the setting or profession of health care, not the healing power of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 描述医疗的场景或职业，而不是某物质本身具有的治疗效力
senses.example: Medical use is the right phrase for a clinic; medicinal use describes a herb that actually heals.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所的用途该说医疗用途；而药用价值说的是某种草药确实能治病。
senses.why: Medicinal arrived first, in the mid-14th century, meaning 'having curative properties'. Medical came later and names the profession, so the pair divides into 'who treats' and 'what cures'.
senses.whyCN: medicinal 先到，14 世纪中叶就有，意为“具有治疗效力的”。medical 来得更晚，命名的是职业，于是这一对词分成“谁来治”与“什么能治”。

intro.en: Medical is a Latin adjective borrowed through French, built on medicus 'physician'. Its root means 'take appropriate measures', not 'middle', and it has no connection with method. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: medical 是经法语借入的拉丁语形容词，建立在 medicus“医生”之上。它的词根意为“采取恰当措施”，不是“中间”，并且与 method 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'pertaining to the art or profession of healing, or to those who practise it'. It came through French médical from Late Latin medicalis 'of a physician'.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 40 年代，意为“与治疗之术或行业、与行医者有关的”。它经法语 médical 来自晚期拉丁语 medicalis“医生的”。

items.en: Latin medicus was both a noun, 'physician, surgeon, medical man', and an adjective, 'healing, medicinal'. It comes from medeor 'to cure, heal', originally 'know the best course for'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 medicus 既是名词“医生、外科医生、医者”，也是形容词“治疗的、药用的”。它来自 medeor“治愈、治疗”，原义为“知道最好的做法”。

items.en: The root *med- means 'take appropriate measures'. De Vaan explains medeor as a shift from 'measure' to 'distribute a cure, heal'; Avestan vi-mad- 'physician' belongs to the same family.
items.cn: 词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”。de Vaan 把 medeor 解释为从“量度”转向“分配药剂、治疗”；阿维斯陀语 vi-mad-“医生”同属这一族。

items.en: The earlier English adjective in this sense was medicinal, 'having healing or curative properties', from Latin medicinalis. Medical later took over the professional sense.
items.cn: 英语中较早表示这一意义的形容词是 medicinal，即“有治疗或治愈效力的”，来自拉丁语 medicinalis。medical 后来接管了职业性的那一层意义。

items.en: The noun is recorded from 1823 colloquially for 'a medical student or practitioner', and from 1917 as a shortening of medical examination.
items.cn: 名词用法 1823 年起有口语记录，指“医科学生或医生”；1917 年起则是 medical examination（体检）的缩略。

items.en: Medical and method share only their letters. Method is Greek methodos, meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road'; no Latin medicus is involved. The -met- shape in the two words is a coincidence, and medicine (c. 1200) likewise comes from medicina, not from medical.
items.cn: medical 与 method 只共享字母外形。method 是希腊语 methodos，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，其中没有任何拉丁语 medicus 的成分。两个词里的 -met- 外形纯属巧合；medicine（约 1200 年）同样来自 medicina，而不是来自 medical。

note.en: The first group is the real medic- family: the substance, the healing property, the act of dosing, and the pills themselves. The second group compares adjectives used in and around health care.
note.cn: 第一组是真正的 medic- 词族：医学本身、治疗效力、用药动作、以及药片本身。第二组比较医疗领域内外的几个形容词。

entries.definition: the science and practice of treating disease, or a substance taken to treat illness. It is the thing and the field; medical is only the adjective that points at them.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗疾病的科学与实践，或用来治病的物质。它是事物与领域本身；medical 只是指向它们的形容词。

entries.definition: having curative properties, or used as a medicine. A medicinal herb heals; a medical herb is merely one a doctor might study.
entries.definitionCN: 具有治疗效力的，或作药用的。medicinal 的草药能治病；medical 的草药只是医生可能会研究的那种草。

entries.definition: to treat with medicine, or to add a drug to something. It names the act that medical describes only indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 用药物治疗，或往某物里加药。它命名的是 medical 只间接描述的那个动作。

entries.definition: a medicinal substance, or the treatment of a condition with drugs. Since 1942 it has been the everyday word for prescribed pills.
entries.definitionCN: 药物，或用药物处理某种病情。自 1942 年起，它成了“处方药”的日常说法。

entries.definition: relating to the observation and treatment of patients, or to a clinic. Clinical stresses the setting and the method; medical stresses the profession as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与病人的观察和治疗有关的，或与诊所相关的。clinical 强调场景与方法；medical 强调整个行业。

entries.definition: relating to the healing of disease, or having a calming or restorative effect. It is closer to medicinal than to medical.
entries.definitionCN: 与疾病治疗有关的，或有镇静、康复效果的。它更接近 medicinal，而不是 medical。

entries.definition: relating to surgery. It is the usual opposite of medical inside a hospital, where medical means treatment by drugs rather than by operation.
entries.definitionCN: 与外科手术有关的。在医院内部它常是 medical 的对立面，那里的 medical 指用药物治疗而非手术。

entries.definition: relating to the auxiliary services that support medical work, such as ambulance crews and lab technicians. The prefix para- 'beside' marks the supporting role.
entries.definitionCN: 与辅助医疗服务有关的，如救护人员与化验员。前缀 para-“在旁边”标记的是支持性的角色。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin medicus 'physician', mederi 'to heal', the older adjective medicinal, and the modern family medicine, medication, medic.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 medicus“医生”、mederi“治疗”、更早的形容词 medicinal，以及现代的 medicine、medication、medic 词族。

normal.en: medic- means 'physician'. Medical is simply the adjective of the doctor's world, as in medical school and medical records.
normal.cn: medic- 表示“医生”。medical 就是医生那个世界的形容词，如 medical school（医学院）、medical records（病历）。

normal.en: The deeper root *med- means 'take appropriate measures'. Healing began as the art of knowing the right measure.
normal.cn: 更深的词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”。治疗最初就是“知道该用多少分量”的技艺。

normal.en: medicinal is older and means 'having healing power'; medical is younger and means 'of the profession'. A medicinal plant heals, a medical student studies.
normal.cn: medicinal 更老，意为“有治疗效力的”；medical 更年轻，意为“属于这一行业的”。药草能治病，医学生则在读书。

normal.en: A medical (noun) is a check-up: the adjective swallowed the noun examination in 1917.
normal.cn: 名词 a medical 就是体检：1917 年这个形容词把名词 examination 吞掉了。

normal.en: Method looks similar but is Greek: meta plus hodos 'road'. Medical has no road in it, only a physician.
normal.cn: method 看着像，其实是希腊语：meta 加 hodos“路”。medical 里面没有路，只有一个医生。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat with two pockets: one holds a stethoscope, the other a folder of records. The coat is medical; the herb in the garden is medicinal.
abstract.cn: 想象一件白大褂有两个口袋：一个装听诊器，一个装一叠病历。这件外套是 medical；园子里的那株草药是 medicinal。

abstract.en: The word always points at people and their apparatus, never at the power of a plant. That is why a hospital is medical and a cough syrup is medicinal.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是指向人及其器械，从不指向植物的效力。所以医院是 medical，止咳糖浆是 medicinal。

abstract.en: A whole institution hides behind three syllables: school, ward, record, certificate, leave. Each is a room the adjective has learned to enter.
abstract.cn: 三个音节背后藏着一整套机构：学院、病房、病历、证明、病假。每一个都是这个形容词学会进入的房间。

examples.en: The village has no medical staff, only a nurse who comes twice a week.
examples.cn: 这个村子没有医务人员，只有一名每周来两次的护士。

examples.en: The insurance company asked for the medical report before paying.
examples.cn: 保险公司在付款前要求提供医学报告。

examples.en: She was on medical leave for a month and came back thinner and quieter.
examples.cn: 她休了一个月病假，回来时瘦了，也沉默了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦迪扣”——麦迪把白大褂的扣子扣好，口袋里插着听诊器 → medical 医疗的、医学的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 medicus“医生”与 mederi“治疗”，词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”，核心是“为身体采取正确的救治手段”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of medical, all radiating from one point: whatever belongs to the physician's world — the school, the ward, the record, the certificate, the machine — and finally the patient's own body as that world describes it.
sensesIntro.cn: medical 的九个义项都从一个点辐射出去：一切属于医生世界的东西——学院、病房、病历、证明、机器——最后是那个世界所描述的病人身体本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white coat whose pockets hold a stethoscope and a folder of records.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件白大褂，口袋里装着听诊器和一叠病历。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: medical names the field and also the drug-treating half of it, set against surgery.
branches.cn: 行业：medical 命名这一领域，也命名其中用药治疗的那一半，与外科相对。

branches.en: THE BODY: the adjective moves from doctors to the patient, naming health, illness and history.
branches.cn: 身体：这个形容词从医生移到病人身上，命名健康、疾病与病史。

branches.en: CLIPPED NOUNS: English shortens 'medical examination' to a medical, and once shortened 'medical man' to the same form.
branches.cn: 截短名词：英语把 medical examination 缩成 a medical，也曾把 medical man 缩成同一个形式。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: law, insurance and employment turn medical into documents, evidence and leave.
branches.cn: 制度：法律、保险与雇佣把 medical 变成文书、证据与病假。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND BOUNDARY: the adjective classifies equipment, and stops short of medicinal, which describes healing power rather than professional setting.
branches.cn: 物件与边界：这个形容词为器械分类，同时止步于 medicinal——后者描述治疗效力，而不是职业场景。

intro.en: Medical is Latin medicus plus the adjective ending -alis, softened in English to -al. The stem medic- is not a free English word, but it carries the whole family.
intro.cn: medical 是拉丁语 medicus 加形容词词尾 -alis，进入英语后软化为 -al。词干 medic- 在英语里不能单独成词，却撑起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin medicus 'physician' and mederi 'to heal' go back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures'. Latin medicina gave English medicine; medicinalis gave medicinal; medicatio gave medication. There is no Greek element in medical.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medicus“医生”与 mederi“治疗”可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当措施”。拉丁语 medicina 给出英语 medicine；medicinalis 给出 medicinal；medicatio 给出 medication。medical 里没有任何希腊语成分。

items.meaning: of or relating to medicine and physicians
items.meaningCN: 医疗的；医学的（medic- 医生 + -al 形容词词尾）
items.example: The medical team arrived before the ambulances.
items.exampleCN: 医疗队在救护车之前就到了。

items.meaningCN: 医学；医术；药物（-ine 构成名词）
items.example: Medicine has changed more in thirty years than in three centuries.
items.exampleCN: 医学在三十年里的变化超过了过去三个世纪。

items.example: The root has a medicinal taste that children hate.
items.exampleCN: 这种根有孩子讨厌的药味。

items.meaningCN: 用药物治疗；给……用药（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The water is medicated with chlorine.

items.meaning: treatment with drugs; a medicinal substance
items.meaningCN: 药物治疗；药物（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: He takes his medication after breakfast.

items.meaning: in medical terms; from a medical point of view
items.meaningCN: 从医学上讲（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The condition is medically unexplained.
items.exampleCN: 这种情况在医学上无法解释。

items.meaning: a doctor, student of medicine, or battlefield medical orderly
items.meaningCN: 医生；医学生；战地卫生员（截短词干）
items.example: A medic stopped the bleeding at the roadside.
items.exampleCN: 一名卫生员在路边止住了血。

items.meaning: relating to biology and medicine together
items.meaningCN: 生物医学的（bio- 生命 + medical）
items.example: The lab won a grant for biomedical research.
items.exampleCN: 该实验室获得了生物医学研究的资助。

items.meaning: supporting medical work without being a doctor
items.meaningCN: 辅助医疗的（para- 在旁边 + medical）
items.example: Paramedical staff handle the first response.
items.exampleCN: 辅助医疗人员负责第一时间的处置。

items.meaning: of the studies taken before medical school
items.meaningCN: 医学预科的（pre- 之前 + medical）
items.example: She finished her premedical courses in two years.
items.exampleCN: 她两年读完了医学预科课程。

items.meaning: a substance used as a remedy
items.meaningCN: 药物；药剂（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: The old pharmacopoeia lists hundreds of medicaments.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧药典列了数百种药剂。

latinEntries.meaning: to cure, heal; originally 'to know the best course for'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 治愈；原义“知道最好的做法”

definition_zh: 药；药物；医学；内科
definition_en: a substance taken to treat or prevent illness, and also the science or practice of healing, including the branch that treats illness without surgery
core_image: 一只棕色玻璃药瓶放在一本翻开的厚医书上，瓶口的软木塞还留着药粉的痕迹
scene: 老式诊所的木架上，一只棕色药瓶和一本翻旧的医书并排放着，瓶身标签已经泛黄。The old doctor said the medicine tasted bitter but worked quickly.
sceneCN: 这里是「药、药物」（第 1 个义项：服用的药）；句意为老医生说这药虽苦却见效快。图中可辨识物件：棕色药瓶、医书、木架。

pos.zh: 药；药物；医学；内科

derivatives.zh: 由 medicine 的词干 medic 加 -al 构成，义为「医学的；医疗的」
由同一词干加 -inal 构成，义为「药用的；有疗效的」
由 medicinal 加 -ly 构成，义为「作为药物地」
由同一词干加 -ment 构成，义为「药物；药剂」

senses.title: A substance taken to treat illness
senses.definition: a substance, especially one taken by mouth, used to treat or prevent illness
senses.definitionCN: 用来治疗或预防疾病的物质，尤指口服的
senses.example: Take this medicine after meals and keep it out of reach of children.
senses.exampleCN: 这药饭后服用，并放在孩子拿不到的地方。
senses.why: Latin medicina first named the healing art, and because the art needed materials, the word came to name the substances themselves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medicina 起初指医术，而医术需要材料，于是这个词也用来指那些材料本身。

senses.title: The science and practice of healing
senses.definition: the science and practice of diagnosing, treating and preventing disease
senses.definitionCN: 诊断、治疗与预防疾病的科学与实践
senses.example: She chose medicine because she wanted to understand how the body fails.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择学医，因为她想弄懂身体是怎样出故障的。
senses.why: The same Latin word named the art of healing as a whole, so the discipline kept the older, broader sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词本就指整体的医术，因此这一学科保留了更早、更宽的含义。

senses.title: The branch that avoids surgery
senses.definition: the branch of medicine that treats disease through drugs and diet rather than surgery
senses.definitionCN: 以药物与饮食而非手术来治病的医学分支，与外科相对
senses.example: He was moved from surgery to medicine when the operation was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 手术取消后，他从外科转到内科。
senses.why: When surgery split off as its own craft, the parent word stayed with the non-surgical side, so medicine also names that department.
senses.whyCN: 当外科独立成一门技艺，母词就留在不动刀的一边，于是 medicine 也指那个科室。

senses.title: Something that improves a bad situation
senses.definition: something that improves a difficult situation, used figuratively as if it were a cure
senses.definitionCN: 比喻能改善困境的事物，好像一剂解药
senses.example: Laughter is good medicine for a tired crew.
senses.exampleCN: 笑声对疲惫的船员是一剂良药。
senses.why: Anything that heals can be called medicine, so the word extends easily from pills to comfort, rest or humour.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能治病的东西都能叫 medicine，于是词义很自然地从药片延伸到安慰、休息或幽默。

intro.en: Medicine goes back to a Latin verb for healing, and the same root produced the doctor, the art and the substances, senses English still keeps apart.
intro.cn: medicine 可追溯到拉丁语表示医治的动词，同一词根生出医生、医术与药物，英语至今把这几个义项分开使用。

items.en: Mederi meant to heal, and it supplied the verb behind physician, remedy and medicine alike.
items.cn: mederi 意为医治，是 physician、remedy 与 medicine 共同的动词来源。

items.en: Medicus was the physician, and medicina was the healing art that this person practised.
items.cn: medicus 指医生，medicina 指这位医生所行的医术。

items.en: Medicina covered both the art of healing and the substances used in it, a double sense from the start.
items.cn: medicina 同时指医术与所用之物，从一开始就是双义。

items.en: Old French medecine kept both senses and handed them to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 medecine 保留这两种含义，并在诺曼时期之后传给英语。

items.en: English medicine now leans on drugs in daily speech, while the discipline and the hospital department keep the older sense.
items.cn: 现代英语里 medicine 在日常口语中偏向药物，而学科与医院科室保留较早的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same healing root; the near-meaning group collects drugs, remedies and forms of care.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「医治」词根的词；近义组收药物、疗法与照护方式。

entries.definition: Having healing properties, used of herbs or substances rather than the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 有疗效的，多用于草药或物质，而非学科。

entries.definition: Relating to the science or practice of healing.
entries.definitionCN: 与医治的科学或实践有关。

entries.definition: A formal term for a substance used to heal.
entries.definitionCN: 指治病物质的正式说法。

entries.definition: Drugs prescribed for a condition, or the course of taking them.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种病情开出的药，或服药的疗程。

entries.definition: A substance used to treat illness or, differently, one taken for pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 用于治病的物质；也可指为快感而用的毒品。

entries.definition: A treatment that cures or relieves a complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 能治愈或缓解病痛的疗法。

entries.definition: A treatment that ends a disease, or the state of being healed.
entries.definitionCN: 终结疾病的疗法；也指痊愈的状态。

entries.definition: A small dose of medicine shaped for swallowing.
entries.definitionCN: 便于吞服的小剂型药物。

entries.definition: The care and procedures used against an illness.
entries.definitionCN: 针对疾病采取的照护与处置。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for healing; its family keeps returning to the doctor, the art, the substance and the department.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示医治的拉丁动词上，同族词反复回到医生、医术、药物与科室。

normal.en: Mederi in Latin means to heal, and medicine is the whole effort built on that verb.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mederi 意为医治，medicine 就是建立在这个动词上的整套努力。

normal.en: Medicus is the doctor; medicina is both the art and what the art uses.
normal.cn: medicus 是医生，medicina 既是医术，也是医术所用的东西。

normal.en: Medical adds -al and describes the field, not a bottle of pills.
normal.cn: medical 加 -al，描述的是这个领域，而不是一瓶药。

normal.en: Medicinal adds -inal and means having the power to heal.
normal.cn: medicinal 加 -inal，意为具有治病效力。

normal.en: The department sense survives in hospital signs, where medicine stands opposite surgery.
normal.cn: 科室义保存在医院标牌上，medicine 与 surgery 相对。

abstract.en: One word holds the art, the pill and the ward, because healing needs knowledge, material and a place to happen.
abstract.cn: 一个词装下了医术、药片与病房，因为治病需要知识、材料与发生的场所。

abstract.en: Calling laughter medicine shows that the word measures not the substance but the relief it brings.
abstract.cn: 把笑声称作良药，说明这个词衡量的不是物质，而是它带来的缓解。

abstract.en: A word that can mean both a science and a bottle reminds us that cure is always part knowledge and part matter.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能指科学又能指药瓶，提醒人治愈总是半靠知识、半靠物质。

examples.en: The medicine worked within an hour and the fever broke.
examples.cn: 药一小时内起效，烧退了。

examples.en: He wants to study medicine in a city hospital.
examples.cn: 他想在城市医院学医。

examples.en: Keep the medicine in a cool, dry place.
examples.cn: 把药放在阴凉干燥处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没事的」——吃了药就没事的；记住 medicine 是药。

root: 拉丁语 mederi（医治）→ medicus（医生）→ medicina（医术、药物），经古法语 medecine 进入英语；同族词多与治疗有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is healing; the senses divide into the substance, the discipline, the hospital branch and the figurative comfort.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是医治；义项分为药物、学科、医院科室与比喻性的安慰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown glass bottle standing on an open medical book, cork still dusted with powder.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只棕色玻璃药瓶放在一本翻开的厚医书上，瓶口的软木塞还留着药粉的痕迹。

branches.en: a spoon of syrup held out to a child
branches.cn: 递到孩子面前的一勺糖浆

branches.en: a laugh that loosens a tense room
branches.cn: 让紧绷的房间松下来的笑声

branches.en: a lecture hall full of diagrams of the body
branches.cn: 挂满人体图的教学厅

branches.en: a hospital corridor sign pointing away from surgery
branches.cn: 医院走廊里指离外科的指示牌

branches.en: a ward round where pills are checked against charts
branches.cn: 按记录核对药片的查房

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of healing, the doctor noun, the noun for the art, the French form and English endings that build adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示医治的拉丁动词、指医生的名词、指医术的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
